name: Almanac
tagline: Warm paper, one green ink, one terracotta word.
jobs: Scrolly explainers, landing pages, long reads, annual reports

tokens.name: paper
tokens.usage: Page ground: warm, uncoated. In Night the ink becomes the ground.

tokens.name: card
tokens.usage: Cards, tickets, dialogs: a lighter sheet on the paper.

tokens.name: band
tokens.usage: The hero band and arch panels: a deeper warm ground that holds one big thing.

tokens.name: screen
tokens.usage: The soft green ground inside a device or a figure.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Hairlines at a quarter strength. The only border in the system.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Forest green: all text, all rules, the first series.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Secondary text at 65%: captions, notes, metadata.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Terracotta: the one word in a headline, the filled button, the progress bar, the second series.

tokens.name: accent-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for accent tags and the selected state.

tokens.name: mauve
tokens.usage: The third series and nothing else.

tokens.name: positive
tokens.usage: Success text and the kept share, with a word.

tokens.name: positive-soft
tokens.usage: Ground for success callouts and positive tags.

tokens.name: caution
tokens.usage: Warnings as text: an ochre on paper.

tokens.name: negative
tokens.usage: Errors share the terracotta; there is no second red.

type_roles.name: display-xl
type_roles.usage: One per page. Instrument Serif at 400 with the tracking pulled tight; the italic carries the emphasised word.

type_roles.name: numeral-xl
type_roles.usage: The outcome numbers. Instrument Serif, tracked to -.07em, one per block.

type_roles.name: body-l
type_roles.sample: Some come back whole. Some give something of themselves.
type_roles.usage: Step paragraphs and lead copy at a generous 1.7 leading.

type_roles.name: body
type_roles.sample: Every device is assessed before its next path is decided.

type_roles.name: label
type_roles.usage: Eyebrows, nav links, legends, chapter numbers. Caps from CSS.

type_roles.name: numeral
type_roles.usage: KPI figures in tiles and tickets.

idea: Almanac is the studio that prints field guides: warm paper, one green ink for everything written, one terracotta word where the eye should land, and hairlines so light they feel drawn. Numbers go enormous in a serif and sit still. Panels have arched tops. Buttons are outlines until you touch them. It is calm without being beige, because the one accent is earned.
use_for: Scrolly explainers, landing pages for small makers and civic things, long reads, annual and impact reports, anything that wants to feel made by hand and read slowly.
avoid_when: Dense operational dashboards, dev tools, anything that must feel fast or cold, and pages that need more than one accent per view.
principles_headline: One ink, one word, one arch.
principles: Text, rules, figures, the first series: all forest green. Colour never carries meaning the ink could carry.
The accent lands on the emphasised word in a headline, the filled button, the second series. Twice on a view is once too many.
Separation is a 1px rule at a quarter strength above a block. Cards are rare and cast a soft terracotta shadow when they exist.
Outcome numbers are set in the serif at -.07em, one per block, with the sentence under them. They are read, not scanned.
A panel with a rounded top holds one object: a device, a figure, a number. Everything else stays on the paper.
voice: Plain, kind, present tense: "Sixty phones return to use."
Numbers spelled in the sentence, set as figures in the block.
Eyebrows in mono caps with a slash: "FIELD NOTES / 001".
Say what is invented: "A fictional workshop story" sits in the hero caption.
colour_headline: Paper, green ink, terracotta, and a mauve for the third series.
colour_note: Paper first. Night turns the ink into the ground and lifts the terracotta so it still lands. There is no blue anywhere; the mauve exists only as a chart series. Status text shares the green and the terracotta; warnings are an ochre. Tags are tints of the same inks.
chart_note: Green, terracotta, mauve: the three outcome colours from the field. Two more only when a chart truly has five series.
type_headline: Instrument Serif for the big and the italic; DM Sans for reading; DM Mono for the small caps.
type_note: Three Google-hosted families. Instrument Serif at 400 (there is no bold) carries display and numerals, tracked tight; the italic is the emphasised word. DM Sans at 400/500 reads at 1.6–1.7 leading. DM Mono at 11px caps carries eyebrows, legends and nav.
space_headline: A generous rhythm: 1.7 leading, 45px gaps, 180px arches.
space: Control padding-y; the dialog action gap.
Default stack gap; unit-field gaps on wide screens are 9–10px.
Ticket and step padding; the summary row.
edges: Buttons, tickets, cards, tiles. Square, with a hairline.
The small shapes in a field: 4px, or 50% 50% 12% 12% for the pip variant.
Panels that hold one thing. The signature edge.
The only border. Above blocks, between details, under the nav.
depth: 23px 23px 0 terracotta at 12%. On the device in a hero and on dialogs. Nothing else floats.
12px 12px 0 at 12% on tickets when they are interactive.
The band and the screen tints stand in for elevation.
motion: Outlined buttons fill with ink and lift 2px, 200ms. The device straightens from its 12° tilt to 3°, 500ms.
Sections and steps use the kit reveal-up at 650ms, 160ms stagger.
Units outside the active outcome fade to 15% and scale to .88 over 600ms. The active ones fill.
A 3px terracotta progress line along the top of the page, driven by scroll in the live reader.
One ambient float at most, on the hero device. No marquee.
Everything visible, nothing moves; the field stays fully filled.
components_headline: The kit on warm paper; the arch, the field and the outline are classes.
components_note: Kit components take Almanac through the contract: paper and card grounds, terracotta primary, band secondary, hairline borders, 4px radius. The outlined button, the arch and the unit field are classes on authored elements: al-btn, al-arch, al-field.
buttons: <Button>Book a place</Button><Button variant="secondary">Read the story</Button><Button variant="outline">Follow the batch</Button><Button variant="ghost">Skip</Button><button className="al-btn al-btn-fill">Book a place</button><button className="al-btn">Follow the batch ↓</button>
buttons_note: Kit buttons on the left; authored al-btn on the right: a 1px outline in ink that fills on hover, text in mono caps, a wide gap before the arrow. The filled variant is terracotta and there is one per view.
tags: KeptBandOutlineLostField notesKeptParts● Returned
tags_note: Tags are mono caps with a hairline, square. Status tags carry a pip or a word with the colour.
fields_note: Fields are the card ground with a hairline; the focus ring is terracotta. Labels are mono caps.
stats:
get another everyday.

of 100 · back in use

help another along.

of 100 · donor parts
stats_note: An outcome block: a hairline on top, the number enormous in the serif, the sentence under it, the share in small text. Three across on wide screens.
callouts:
A fictional workshop storyThe batch is invented; every figure is shown as arithmetic.
Note. A fact about the batch, set between two hairlines.
Booked. Your place on Saturday is held.
No places left. The next workshop opens on the 24th.
callouts_note: A callout is text between two hairlines, with a soft tint when it carries status. The text stays ink.
chart_comp_note: Charts take green, terracotta and mauve in that order. Bars are flat; lines are ink at 2px; axes are hairlines.
table_note: Tables are ink on paper with hairline rows and serif figures; no container border.
card:
Saturday workshop

Repair with us · places are free

DateSat 10 Oct · 10:00
Places of 20 left
card_note: A ticket: the card ground, a serif title, details between hairlines, two buttons. It casts the soft shadow only when it opens as a dialog.

hand.headline: Flat ink, hairline edges, a shadow you can see through.
hand.note: Almanac draws any subject with flat fills in green and terracotta, 1.5px ink outlines with round caps, and a terracotta shadow at 12% slipped 6px behind the main body. Small things are rounded; big panels get an arch. No gradients, no texture; the warmth comes from the paper and the ink.
rules: 1.5px forest green, round caps and joins.
Flat green for the main share, terracotta for the second, paper-sunk for the rest.
Terracotta at 12%, offset 6px, only behind the main body.
Small shapes 4–6px or pill; panels arched 180px at the top.
DM Mono caps at 11px; Instrument Serif for the one number.
The drawing may float once or tilt 12° and straighten on hover.

motifs_headline: The arch, the field, and the ticket.
motifs_note: Three devices from the field guide: a panel that holds one thing, a hundred small shapes that show a share, and a card whose details sit between hairlines. Each is drawn with the hand variables, so it ports.

motifs.title: The arch
motifs.usage: A panel with a 180px rounded top on the band ground, one object centred inside, the soft shadow slipped behind. Use it for the hero device, a figure, or one big number.

dos: One terracotta word per headline; the rest stays green.
Hairlines above blocks, never boxes around them.
Numbers enormous in the serif, with the sentence underneath.
Hold one thing in an arch; leave the rest on the paper.
donts: No bold serif (there is none); emphasis is the italic.
No blue, no second red; mauve is a chart series only.
No drop shadows except the terracotta one at 12%.
No more than one filled button per view.
binding_losses: The arch, the translucent offset shadow, the hairline-at-a-quarter rule, the band and screen grounds, and the unit field have no contract slot. They are carried as --ds-* properties and the al-* classes above; kit components take paper, ink and terracotta but stay square.
footer: Paper first, Night second. Fonts: Instrument Serif 400 + italic, DM Sans 400/500/700, DM Mono 400/500, Google-hosted.

tpl.slide_sub: One hundred tools, three paths, and the weekend they gave back.
tpl.slide_body: Of every hundred tools lent out, this many came back whole and went straight back on the shelf.
tpl.ed_deck: Some come back whole. Some give something of themselves. Every tool in the shed has a next destination, and this is how a hundred of them found theirs.
tpl.ed_byline: Words and pictures: the shed · a fictional story
tpl.ed_body: The shed takes in a hundred tools a season. Each one is assessed on a Saturday before its next path is decided: back on the shelf, into the parts drawer, or off to the recycler. Sixty come back whole after a clean and an oiling. Twenty-five give a motor or a battery to another tool. Fifteen are simply done, and they leave as clean metal.
steps: A hundred tools arrive over a season. Each small shape is one of them; nothing is decided yet.
They come back whole: cleaned, oiled, reshelved. Their story continues as complete tools.
